title: Kratos Receives $33.6 Million Contract to Provide Power Conversion System for NASA’s Historic SR-1 Freedom Nuclear-Powered Spacecraft
summary: Kratos announced a $33.6 million contract award to design, build, and deliver the power conversion system for NASA’s Space Reactor-1 Freedom.
body_markdown:
**Targeted for Launch in 2028, Freedom Will Be the First U.S. Nuclear Fission Reactor-Powered Interplanetary Spacecraft**


SAN DIEGO, Oct. 28, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) — Kratos Defense & Security Solutions, Inc. (Nasdaq: KTOS), a leading technology company in the defense, national security, and space domains, today announced a $33.6 million contract award to design, build, and deliver the power conversion system for NASA’s Space Reactor-1 Freedom. Kratos will be executing this work as a subcontractor to Sierra Lobo, Inc., under their NASA SpaceDOC III contract. Targeted for launch in 2028, SR-1 Freedom will be the first nuclear fission reactor-powered interplanetary spacecraft, designed to travel beyond Earth’s orbit to Mars, demonstrate advanced nuclear electric propulsion (NEP), and successfully deliver the SkyFall payload.


*Space Reactor-1 Freedom will be the first spacecraft ever to demonstrate fission power beyond Earth’s orbit, traveling to Mars to deliver a sciece payload called SkyFall.* *Photo Credit: NASA/Alberto Bertolin*


Under this subcontract, Kratos will provide a compact, space-qualified closed Brayton cycle power conversion system. This crucial component serves as the mechanical bridge between SR-1 Freedom’s onboard fission reactor and the spacecraft’s power distribution and electric propulsion subsystems. It converts the thermal energy generated by the reactor into the vital electrical power required to drive SR-1’s propulsion thrusters and sustain all critical spacecraft operations.


Nuclear electric propulsion utilizes a fission-based, nuclear power module to generate electricity, powering highly efficient electric thrusters rather than relying solely on conventional chemical thrusters. By accelerating charged particles to create a gentle but relentless thrust, NEP allows the spacecraft to gradually build immense velocity. Because they can operate continuously for months or years, NEP-equipped spacecraft can reach Mars utilizing significantly less propellant than traditional chemically propelled spacecraft. This unprecedented efficiency drastically reduces fuel requirements, freeing up critical mass for scientific instruments, cargo, and future crew-support equipment.


“Being selected to power SR-1 Freedom is a generational honor for Kratos,” said **Stacey Rock, President of Kratos Turbine Technologies Division** . “SR-1 is the spacecraft that turns space nuclear propulsion from concept into reality; it is the vehicle that will help answer whether America leads the third space race or watches it from the sidelines. By delivering the power conversion heart of SR-1 Freedom, Kratos is helping NASA give birth to the ‘Nuclear NASA’ that will open the outer solar system, shorten the path to Mars, and strengthen our national security in space.”


NASA has positioned the SR-1 Freedom mission as a cornerstone in a broader space nuclear initiative. The mission aims to launch the first U.S. space reactor since 1965, paving the way for a transformative era of deep space exploration. SR-1 Freedom is strategically structured to mitigate development risks and cultivate the necessary industrial base for future deep-space operations and will facilitate follow-on concepts like Lunar Reactor-1 (LR-1), which is envisioned as a sun-independent power source for NASA’s upcoming Moon Base efforts. The SR-1 Freedom contract adds to Kratos’ expanding portfolio of advanced propulsion, power, and hypersonics work. This milestone reinforces the company’s broader corporate strategy of leveraging strategic internal investments to support critical national security and next-generation space programs.

**About Kratos Defense & Security Solutions**
Kratos Defense & Security Solutions, Inc. (NASDAQ: KTOS) is a technology, products, system and software company addressing the defense, national security, and commercial markets. Kratos makes true internally funded research, development, capital and other investments, to rapidly develop, produce and field solutions that address our customers’ mission critical needs and requirements. At Kratos, affordability is a technology, and we seek to utilize proven, leading-edge approaches and technology, not unproven bleeding edge approaches or technology, with Kratos’ approach designed to reduce cost, schedule and risk, enabling us to be first to market with cost effective solutions. We believe that Kratos is known as an innovative disruptive change agent in the industry, a company that is an expert in designing products and systems up front for successful rapid, large quantity, low-cost future manufacturing which is a value-add competitive differentiator for our large traditional prime system integrator partners and also to our government and commercial customers. Kratos intends to pursue program and contract opportunities as the prime or lead contractor when we believe that our probability of win (PWin) is high and any investment required by Kratos is within our capital resource comfort level. We intend to partner and team with a large, traditional system integrator when our assessment of PWin is greater or required investment is beyond Kratos’ comfort level. Kratos’ primary business areas include virtualized ground systems for satellites and space vehicles including software for command & control (C2) and telemetry, tracking and control (TT&C), jet powered unmanned aerial drone systems, hypersonic vehicles and rocket systems, propulsion systems for drones, missiles, loitering munitions, supersonic systems, space craft and launch systems, C5ISR and microwave electronic products for missile, radar, missile defense, space, satellite, counter UAS, directed energy, communication and other systems, and virtual & augmented reality training systems for the warfighter.
